n.exclusions: Preregistered eligibility, completion and attention checks; see report Sample and protocol deviations.
n.quote: Replication results: In the replication experiment, participants behaved in an uncalculating manner in the process observable condition (when their reputation is at stake) with a probability of 0.190 (se = 0.013; n = 920), while participants in the process hidden condition behaved in an uncalculating manner (when their reputation is not at stake) with a probability of 0.171 (se = 0.013; n = 906). This difference was tested using a logistic regression (b = –0.129, se = 0.122; z = 1.062, p = 0.288; n = 1826). As a result, participants were not more likely to behave in an uncalculating manner in the process observable condition than in the process hidden condition. The standardized effect size (Cohen’s d) is d = 0.050 (95% CI [–0.042, 0.141]).
